entries.title: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps.
entries.summary: Google and Adobe are integrating creative and productivity tools. Edit PDFs in Drive and use Adobe AI in Gemini. See what’s new in this partnership.
entries.content:
Today at Adobe MAX, we announced we’re expanding our partnership with Adobe.

Switching between apps to edit a PDF or fine-tune an image can quickly break your focus. Our partnership will bring Adobe’s creative and productivity tools directly into the Google products you use every day. It will also bring Google’s frontier AI models into Adobe’s apps. Here’s what’s coming:

  • Work faster with PDFs: You’ll soon have a direct pathway from Google Drive and Gmail into Adobe Acrobat, surfaced as a suggested app across both services, including an “Edit with” entry point in file previews.
  • Create right where you search and chat: Adobe is expanding its connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise with Acrobat and additional creative tools. Adobe will also bring its creative tools to AI Mode in Google Search.
  • Powering creatives and enterprises: Businesses will be able to use Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker agent in Gemini Enterprise — an AI assistant that helps teams design graphics, work with PDFs, and launch marketing campaigns without switching apps.
  • Exploring editing experiences with DeepMind: Adobe and Google DeepMind will explore new editing capabilities for creative professionals, starting with an image model for Photoshop that could enable near-real-time edits.

entries.title: 40 years of American culinary history with the James Beard Foundation
entries.summary: Hero image for the 'Bite by Bite' project featuring a background collage of historical menus overlaid with the project logo and the text: 'Discover over 40 years of USA's culinary trends through 10,000 menus'
entries.content:
Dive into American culinary history like never before, thanks to a new partnership between the James Beard Foundation and Google Arts & Culture: Bite by Bite.

For over four decades, the James Beard Foundation — a launchpad for many of today’s top chefs — has hosted dinners capturing the evolution of American cuisine. This new James Beard Foundation digital archive opens a window into that evolution, with an interactive experiment and more than 10,000 digitized menus from those dinners documenting how ingredients, trends, and values have shifted across generations.

Mapping 40 years of food trends

The James Beard Menu Archive makes thousands of menus easy to explore and learn from. It uses AI to analyze ingredients across decades, letting you discover how dining habits have changed, from the explosion of kale in the 2000s to the decline of foie gras. More than just lists of dishes, the menus serve as cultural time capsules, revealing what diners valued at exact moments in history, how sourcing has evolved, and how regional and global influences have reshaped American dining.

Beyond the menus, the archive also features a curated story series that spotlights James Beard, “the father of American gastronomy,” the history of the James Beard Foundation’s New York City headquarters, and more.

Listening to voices from the culinary community

Regarding this project, James Beard Award–winning chef Marcus Samuelsson says that food connects diverse communities. The collaboration celebrates the people behind every plate and honors their cultures and innovations. By bringing their heritage online and opening the archive to kitchens everywhere, we hope to inspire the next generation of culinary creatives.

Immerse yourself in American culinary history by exploring the James Beard Foundation on Google Arts & Culture.

entries.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
entries.summary: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare to unify clinical data and automate workflows. Reduce administrative burnout. See how it works.
entries.content:
Google Cloud has announced Gemini for healthcare, an AI solution engineered to unify fragmented clinical, operational, and administrative systems. Moving beyond simple information retrieval, it enables healthcare teams to turn siloed data into coordinated action.

Clinicians lose nearly 28 hours each week to paperwork and administrative tasks, fueling burnout and straining budgets. By integrating specialized skills and data connectors with existing third-party systems, the platform brings together critical information from electronic health records, billing platforms, clinical guidelines, and Medicare datasets.

Gemini for healthcare reasons across this context to orchestrate and execute complex, multi-step workflows — such as medical records synthesis and prior authorization review — within defined guardrails and with appropriate human oversight. Initially available in preview alongside launch partners including HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health, and Northwell Health, it resolves bottlenecks and reclaims valuable staff time for patient care. Learn more on the Cloud blog.

entries.title: Waze and Garmin team up to boost driver awareness of cyclists.
entries.summary: Waze and Garmin improve road safety with real-time cycling alerts. See how Garmin LiveTrack icons help drivers stay aware of nearby cyclists. Get the details.
entries.content:
Waze and Garmin are launching real-time cycling alerts to help create a safer environment on the road.

Now, when cyclists turn on Garmin LiveTrack™ on their Garmin Edge® bike computer or Garmin smartwatch, they can choose to show up as a real-time, moving icon on Waze for extra peace of mind. Drivers will also see a notification when a cyclist is nearby, giving them a helpful reminder to slow down, stay aware, and share the road thoughtfully.

This feature is completely opt-in and built with privacy in mind. Drivers only see a temporary alert that a cyclist is nearby — never information about a specific cyclist or route. Plus, alerts automatically turn off the moment a cyclist ends their ride on their Garmin device.

Cycling alerts powered by Garmin are rolling out now globally on Android and iOS.

entries.title: Developers can now build with Google Maps Platform in AI Studio.
entries.summary: Developers can now build with Google Maps Platform in AI Studio.
entries.content:
Building real-world context into your apps just got much easier. You can now use Google Maps Platform directly inside Google AI Studio, eliminating the need to leave your workspace to configure billing and credentials. Jump in and try it at no cost.

How it works:

  • Describe your idea: Head to AI Studio and prompt Gemini with any real-world concept (e.g., "Build an interactive 3D tour of NYC showcasing iconic landmarks").
  • Enable Google Maps seamlessly: Get started in minutes with no credit cards required, 1 or let AI Studio automatically detect and link your existing Google Cloud project.
  • Watch it come to life: AI Studio securely connects your key and instantly loads a live, interactive preview.

Try it out today in AI Studio or read the full announcement on the Google for Developers blog.

entries.title: Our newest TPUs: 8tx and 8i Max, built for the agentic era
entries.content:
We first designed TPUs more than a decade ago motivated by Google’s internal demands, including voice recognition and language translation. Eight generations of TPUs later, the use cases have exploded, covering: i) training and serving our own Gemini models, ii) agentic workloads, iii) delivering services to Google Cloud customers on our cloud infrastructure, and most recently, iv) allowing customers to deploy TPUs directly into their own data centers. TPUs are now a rapidly growing business with nearly 100 customers — including frontier labs, trading firms, retailers, universities, and more.

At Google Cloud Next in April, we introduced two new specialized TPUs in the same generation — 8t for large-scale training and 8i for real-time reasoning. TPU 8t and 8i offer up to 2.7 times better training performance and 80% better inference price performance, respectively, versus our previous generation of TPUs.

Today, we’re taking that a step further, expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two additional systems: TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack, and TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference. This is the first time we have introduced four TPU systems in a single year.

Our expanded eighth-generation TPU portfolio: TPU 8t, TPU 8i, TPU 8tx, and TPU 8i Max.

While we’ve always co-designed our TPUs in partnership with Google DeepMind, we’re now increasingly getting feedback from external organizations on their specific needs. With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows. In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads.

The new TPU systems we are announcing today address this new reality. Coupled with our recent PyTorch announcements, our aim is to make TPUs more easily accessible to every developer and Cloud customer. By combining modular custom silicon with an open and easy-to-use software stack, we can deliver new hardware and system configurations at the pace of the AI industry.

Building the computer around the chip

Today, we’re announcing two new TPU systems — and there’s an important difference between a new chip and a new system.

Designing a new chip means laying out billions of microscopic transistors on a silicon wafer in a multi-year process bound by the laws of physics and a complex, long-duration manufacturing lifecycle. A system, on the other hand, is about how we bring together the compute, networking, and storage around the chip. This can include how they are packaged with the chips, to quickly meet emerging customer needs and research use cases.

When we built our very first TPU more than a decade ago, we knew AI software would evolve much faster than silicon manufacturing ever could. So we made a foundational bet on system balance and modularity, architecting our TPUs as building blocks as part of our AI Hypercomputer, so engineers could rapidly adjust packaging, high-speed memory, optical networking, and security around them. That approach allows us to deliver specialized supercomputers in a matter of months rather than years.

Specializing for secure, high-context AI

Each system in our eighth-generation TPU portfolio targets a distinct part of the AI lifecycle.

TPU 8t and TPU 8i established the baseline for this generation of chips:

  • TPU 8t was designed to be a training powerhouse for massive foundation models with maximum “goodput” — or the useful intelligence delivered per watt of energy used.
  • TPU 8i is the reasoning engine, designed to break the memory wall, cutting inter-chip communication delays by up to half.

Now, as enterprises bring autonomous agents into production, we have created two new configurations of these foundational systems to solve two urgent new challenges: hardware-level data security and million-token context scale.

TPU 8tx

TPU 8tx, our third eighth-generation system, is optimized for secure and confidential inference and is also great for small-scale training. It’s built for regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models and autonomous agents alongside their most sensitive data.

Normally, data is encrypted when stored or sent over a network, but has to be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. Built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and paired with 5th Generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts, TPU 8tx builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use. And by adopting the same low-latency Boardfly network we created for real-time reasoning, TPU 8tx keeps multi-step agents moving, delivering up to 2x lower latency compared to TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty.

Pairing training-grade compute with a fast inference network also means organizations can simultaneously run and customize their models on a single system. TPU 8tx enables teams to fine-tune models using their private data, distill large models into smaller ones, and train their agents through reinforcement learning, all without needing to migrate sensitive data between separate clusters.

Designed for sensitive enterprise workloads, TPU 8tx provides hardware-level confidential compute for private fine-tuning and secure agent execution.

TPU 8i Max

Our fourth system, TPU 8i Max, is built for a different problem: the memory wall.

When dozens of AI agents work together across an entire software codebase or hours of video at once, memory bandwidth quickly becomes the bottleneck. So we took two low-latency TPU 8i chips and combined them onto a single package.

TPU 8i Max scales compute and memory in lockstep, delivering double the compute, double the SRAM and double the HBM bandwidth of TPU 8i, so processors remain equipped with essential data and so that large workloads do not stall. Further, because TPU 8i Max fits twice the silicon within the existing rack footprint, data centers can deploy significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt.

The dual-chip TPU 8i Max system, engineered for massive context windows and maximum compute density.

While flexible across workloads, together the four systems in our eighth-generation TPUs give customers a purpose-built accelerator for every stage of the agentic lifecycle. TPU 8t for scale-up training, TPU 8i for low-latency reasoning, TPU 8tx for confidential computing, and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack.

Opening up TPUs to every developer

When we launched the first TPU more than a decade ago, there were only a handful of companies running workloads that needed the processing power of a TPU. The use cases were specialized, so engineers would use optimized frameworks and hand-tuned code.

Over the years, as AI has advanced, more and more companies began using accelerators. Now, AI adoption is at a point where TPUs are excellent for a wide range of companies and use cases, and as a result, we’ve been working systematically to remove barriers to adoption so that TPUs are as easy-to-use as general-purpose hardware.

This investment comes together today across these key areas:

  • Opening up TPU development to every PyTorch developer; no code rewrites needed: Last month, we open-sourced TorchTPU, so PyTorch code and Hugging Face models now run natively on TPUs, alongside out-of-the-box TPU backends for leading open-source inference engines like vLLM and SGLang. And to make hardware optimization effortless, our new open-source TPU agent suite (now in preview) plugs directly into coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Google Antigravity to automate TPU onboarding in minutes, diagnose bottlenecks, and autotune custom kernels using plain language. For production deployments, our new open-source XLA Serving Engine lets you train models in Python and serve them directly in a low-latency C++ runtime across TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs.
  • Industry-leading production performance on InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks:

    In production, what really matters is outcomes on real AI workloads rather than theoretical peak chip speeds. On industry-standard InferenceX and AgentXbenchmarks, which test realistic agentic coding and long-context work, our native vLLM-TorchTPU software stack on TPUs achieved state-of-the-art price-performance marks. New evaluations demonstrate these advantages extend across a wide range of frontier open models and open-source serving stacks while maintaining high model accuracy. Upcoming software optimizations on this same hardware will drive those results even further.
  • Eliminating idle compute waste for autonomous agents: Because AI agents are stateful, they frequently pause for seconds or hours while waiting on a database lookup, an external software tool, or human feedback. To make our agents more resource-efficient during those pauses, our new Agent Compute Engine software automatically suspends and resumes idle sessions, cutting operational infrastructure costs.
  • Breaking through the memory wall with the model-state layer (TPU Sync): Building the computer around the chip also means unifying memory, storage, and networking in software. As agents reason across million-token contexts and continuous reinforcement learning (RL) loops, memory quickly becomes the bottleneck. We’re open-sourcing TPU Sync, the model-state layer for TPU clusters. TPU Sync turns chip HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network into a single, co-designed memory hierarchy — automatically tiering massive KV caches off the chip in milliseconds, streaming context across disaggregated prefill and decode nodes, and synchronizing RL weights to cut KV transfer latency and Time to First Token (TTFT) by more than 90%.
  • Scaling distributed workloads across TPUs from a single controller: Now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Cloud Pathways brings the Google DeepMind runtime behind Gemini to every Google Cloud customer. Using a single-controller architecture and pathwaysutils, you can orchestrate large-scale TPU systems across multiple slices as if they were one local machine for pre-training, reinforcement learning, and multihost inference. Cloud Pathways keeps long-running jobs moving through hardware disruptions with colocated Python sidecars, sub-minute slice hot-swapping, and elastic resharding.
  • Stitching custom TPU topologies on-demand with GKE dynamic slicing: Now generally available, GKE dynamic slicing decouples physical hardware provisioning from logical slice formation using optical circuit switching (OCS) technology. By dynamically assembling TPU cubes into larger topologies (super-slicing) or partitioning them into smaller, isolated workloads (sub-slicing) on-the-fly, this update completely eliminates rigid, manual nodepool recreation cycles. This topology agility slashes job startup times by up to 5x and accelerates fault recovery by up to 4.5x, maximizing overall fleet utilization and workload goodput across all TPUs.

Co-designing with a decade of experience

Shipping four TPU systems and a unified, open software stack in a single year only happens when silicon architects, networking engineers, compiler teams, and Google DeepMind researchers build side-by-side.

Increasingly, we’re even tapping into AI to ideate and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. From using Google DeepMind’s AlphaChip reinforcement learning system to using Gemini to deliver chip layouts in hours rather than weeks, we’re using TPU-powered AI services to rapidly accelerate next-generation TPU hardware development. This is true co-design and a unique Google differentiator.

Learn more about our new TPU systems by tuning into today’s broadcast at 9 a.m. PT.

entries.title: Holiday 100: Your guide to this year’s top trending gifts
entries.summary: Text "Holiday 100" surrounded by various products: a piano keyboard mat, a camera, a pair of jeans, a kettle, a suitcase, a vase, and a tube of lipstick. In the top right is a bow.
entries.content:
Finding a gift that feels thoughtful can feel like a full-time job. Whether you’re shopping for your little sibling who has everything, your friend with impossibly cool taste, or your partner who insists they don’t need anything, we’ve got you covered.

Today, we’re sharing our annual Holiday 100, a curated gift guide based on this year’s Search trends across tech, home, style, beauty, toys, and more. With over a billion searches related to shopping every day 1 , we get a front-row seat to what’s actually topping everyone’s wish lists. From viral sensations that broke the internet to nostalgic styles making a massive comeback, here is inspiration for your holiday shopping and a look at what people are searching for:

  • Step out in style: The kitten heel renaissance is in full swing; searches for “kitten heel sandals” strutted up 295%.
  • Throwback kicks hit stride: Queries for “nike v5 rnr running shoes” climbed 150% in 2026.
  • The ultimate layering piece: Utilitarian style peaked as “utility jacket” was searched more than ever.
  • A signature scent: Perfume officially claimed the top type of gift sets searched this year.
  • Roll into retro fun: Searches for “adjustable roller skates” cruised up 180%.
  • Bring the spa home: Facial wellness tools had a massive breakout year, with search interest in “lymphatic sculpting face brush” spiking by 400%.
  • Good hair days ahead: Searches for “cécred hair products” grew 160% in 2026.
  • Sound like a studio pro: Creative side-hustles leveled up, driving a 115% surge in searches for "podcast microphone."
  • Cozy season in a cup: Searches for “ski mug” was a breakout search this year.
  • Spark timeless holiday wonder: Some traditions never fade, with queries for “classic toy train set” skyrocketing 240% to bring magic under the tree.

For more gift ideas, explore the full Holiday 100 list today. Visit g.co/holiday100 and make this holiday season your most effortless yet.

Happy shopping (and treat yourself to a little something, too)!

entries.title: Generate longer AI videos with Omni 1.2 Flash in Google Vids at no cost.
entries.content:
Google Vids, our video creation and editing tool, now runs on Google's newest video generation model: Omni 1.2 Flash. Starting today, anyone with a Google account or Google Workspace subscription can generate up to three 15-second videos per month in Vids at no cost.

With Omni 1.2 in Google Vids, you can now bring your ideas to life in so many more ways:

  • Create your product promos in one go. Produce professional, quick-turn social content and promotional materials without a single cut.
  • Transform static imagery into engaging videos. Upload reference images from anything — a trip, a school project, or learning materials — and your characters and scenes will stay consistent, from the first frame to the last.
  • Make clips that sound more natural. With improved speech narration, your social clips, concept explainers, and teaser videos feel like something you recorded yourself.

If you can describe it, you can make it. Try Google Vids out at vids.new.

entries.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
entries.summary: Text "Gemini Introducing Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash" surroudned by images of a beehive, animals in conversation, a squid, and a woman walking down a street
entries.content:
Today, we’re rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing capabilities, and enhanced reference following. We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1 making it available at $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Here’s an overview of what’s new:

Fast and cost-effective at scale

Beyond the lower price, the workflow keeps costs down: you can draft fast at 360p or 720p, fix a detail with a follow-up edit instead of re-generating the entire clip, and then upscale your best creations to 1080p or 4K.

Longer clips up to 15 seconds

You can now generate and edit videos natively up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds with Omni 1.1. You can also specify duration in one-second increments from 3 to 15 seconds, giving you room to tell complete stories, create product explainers, or produce full social ad spots in a single generation.

Better reference adherence

You can guide generation combining character, product, or style images, short motion clips (up to three seconds), and audio cues — and Omni 1.2 Flash holds onto those details from start to finish. Faces, garments, packaging typography, and brand colors stay consistent across camera angles, making it easy to turn existing product photography or character sheets into virtual try-on clips, catalog spins, and branded video ads.

Combining one model photo with front-and-back product shots of three outfits, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates a 15-second virtual try-on sequence across 360-degree turns and match cuts while keeping the model’s identity and each garment’s cut, drape, and back details consistent.

More consistent results

You can maintain stronger character, object, and scene consistency from the first to the last frame, with less visual drift or morphing across motion and camera transitions. Whether you’re interpolating between a first and last keyframe, or extending a clip to build a longer sequence, products, characters, props, and environments stay consistent from shot to shot.

Given the same static studio lighting exhibition poster and five-layer animation prompt, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash does not match the reference image as closely as 1.2 does. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash builds the poster sequentially layer by layer on the dusty-pink cyclorama rising the hexagonal plinth, assembling the ribbed glass, warm filament, faceted crystal, and coiled-cord letterforms for HALO, GLOW, and LUMEN, and locking every material, shadow, and typographic detail consistently through the final frame.

Easier editing in conversation

You can refine the same clip turn by turn — such as swapping a product or background, changing the lighting or weather, or switching the aspect ratio — instead of starting over from scratch. Multi-turn conversational editing works across full 15-second clips, making it easy to produce ad variants for different audiences and placements without re-briefing or re-generating.

Starting from one generated clip, multi-turn conversational prompts swap the background turn by turn — from a striped pavilion tent to an oak forest, a stable with a white horse, a market fair, and a stone castle — while keeping both characters’ performances, armor reflections, and camera framing intact.

More natural speech

You can generate scenes with more fluid, natural-sounding dialogue, clearer lip-sync, and distinct multi-speaker conditioning. This will show up whether you’re directing multi-character dialogue in Flow, creating video explainers in Gemini for business, or creating polished, pro videos with avatars, music and narration in Google Vids.

Conditioned on one conservatory scene image alongside four character, mouth, and one-second voice references, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash routes each sampled voice to the right character with expressive lip-sync and natural comedic timing across a 15-second animated scene.

More controllable, cinematic look

You can direct complex, continuous camera movements like sweeping FPV flythroughs to dramatic zoom-outs and orbits with significantly fewer unwanted jump cuts, steadier scale, and a more polished, cinematic look.

Guided by two architectural reference photos, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash directs one continuous FPV drone flight across the piazza, through the bronze doors, and up through the Pantheon’s coffered dome to the oculus with zero jump cuts.

Longer clips with smoother motion and tighter consistency

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates clips up to 15 seconds long that hold references together better than before. You can scroll through to see characters, text, and camera moves stay consistent across longer shots, multiple turns and transitions with no cuts.

Real-world results, from creatives to global brands

Businesses, startups, and creatives are already using Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash in their workflows. And for the first time, Gemini Omni is now generally available, backed by Google Cloud’s enterprise-grade infrastructure and security. Provisioned Throughput is available, and outputs carry an imperceptible SynthID watermark.

Get started with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash

While development is ongoing to further improve things like fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is ideal for businesses, developers, and creators producing videos at scale. You can get started with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash today as it rolls out across Google’s products and developer platforms:

  • For developers using the Gemini API: Prototype in Google AI Studio, explore interactive starter apps, and check out the developer documentation and pricing.
  • For businesses: Try it in the Google Cloud console, and build enterprise solutions with the API.
  • For everyone using Google apps: Direct scenes and multi-turn edits in Flow, generate 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids with a Google account or Google Workspace subscription, create 15-second videos in the Gemini app (rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers), and scale video campaigns in Google Ads.

entries.title: Investing in Wyoming’s infrastructure, energy and workforce
entries.summary: Community members playing with a pumpkin
entries.content:
Today, we are announcing our first data center in the state of Wyoming, in partnership with Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power (AEP), and Related Digital. Google is making a long-term, $17 billion investment in the Cowboy State, designed to deliver lasting benefits for Laramie County families and businesses.

Our commitment to responsible growth

We’re committed to partnering with communities to build data centers the right way. We will pay for 100% of the power we use, and when we build data centers, we’ll cover the infrastructure needs directly driven by our growth.

The project is contracted with AEP to feature a first-of-its-kind, commercial-scale, 702 MW fuel cell development with carbon capture and storage (CCS) — the largest planned development of its kind to date. Fuel cells efficiently convert fuel, in this case natural gas, into electricity through a safe electrochemical reaction. The fuel cells for this project will be made in America by Bloom Energy and will help minimize emissions and water use in the production of energy for our data infrastructure.

The CCS technology will enable the capture and permanent geologic storage of a large majority of its carbon emissions at Tallgrass’s nearby Eastern Wyoming Sequestration Hub. This project builds on our first CCS project in the U.S. announced last fall, and brings our total contracted CCS capacity to nearly 1 gigawatt.

We are also sourcing power from gas generators operated by Tallgrass Energy and Black Hills Energy, and conducting a technical front-end engineering and design (FEED) study to evaluate fitting Tallgrass’s combined cycle turbines with CCS technology. Together, these efforts represent a novel approach to powering data centers efficiently, accelerating the commercialization of CCS, and creating pathways to reduce the carbon emissions associated with natural gas generation.

Water is another essential shared resource, and we remain deeply committed to using it responsibly and investing in local water replenishment efforts. Consistent with our water stewardship commitments for local communities, our Wyoming data center will be air-cooled to minimize strain on local water resources.

Investment in Cheyenne

We know being a part of the community means investing in the things that matter most to the people in it. Google and our partners have held numerous meetings, and are continuously engaging key stakeholders at the local and state level. Recently, we hosted a community meeting in downtown Cheyenne; we spoke to and met with more than 200 residents in Laramie County, gathering clear and constructive feedback on their priorities. Those include:

A holistic picture of the economic benefits of this project. We expect this project to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in local property taxes for Laramie County and School District 1. This is in addition to our community investment plans, which will focus on initiatives in K-12 education, workforce development, and pathways to accelerate Wyoming’s economy.

Requests for more information on career and job skilling opportunities. Through targeted grants, Google is partnering with key local institutions championing STEM education, supporting local entrepreneurs, and expanding skilled trades training across the state. We already hosted our first Community Day at the Cheyenne Children’s Museum, and we look forward to sharing more about our community partnerships in the coming weeks.

Data center growth supporting communities. A key concern from the community meeting stretches beyond the boundaries of our own project — how data center growth is impacting Cheyenne as a community. Building on our existing engagement efforts, Google, Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, Related Digital, AEP, and Bloom Energy are standing up a Community Council designed to develop common-sense solutions to support Cheyenne through this phase of growth.

Data centers power the technology America relies on — everything from online banking, to digital maps and wayfinding, to hospitals and 911 systems. Building on Google’s 20-year track record of data center development, our promise is to show up today and tomorrow for Cowboy State residents. We are excited to put down roots in Wyoming and look forward to working closely with the community for decades to come.
